descriptor: Pharma excipient (MCC) maker adding specialty disintegrants
lede: An Ahmedabad maker of microcrystalline cellulose (MCC), the filler and binder in most tablets, exporting about two-thirds of its output to 75+ countries. Both plants are full, so it trades bought-in MCC to keep customers while a new Unit III adds higher-value disintegrants (CCS, SSG, pulp-based CMC) and more MCC. Profit and margins are rising fast, but Unit III has missed four start dates and about half of FY26 traded purchases came from promoter-linked firms.

short_version.text: FY26 revenue ₹349 Cr (+32%), PAT ₹44 Cr; H1 FY27 revenue +25% and PAT +72% with EBITDA margin at 25%. Debt-free, receivable days halved to 47, and operating cash flow ₹78 Cr in H1. Unit III could add ₹150-160 Cr (Phase 1) and ₹220-250 Cr (Phase 2) of revenue at peak.

Unit III Phase 1 was due Sep-Oct 2025 and is still waiting for approvals in Oct 2026; Phase 2 slipped from Jun 2026 to H1 FY28. ₹46 Cr of FY26 purchases were from promoter-linked firms, promoters cut their stake from 55.5% to 51.4% in six months, and management says it gives no guidance.
~28x trailing earnings and ~22x EV/EBITDA; Nitta Gelatin trades at 14x and Fine Organic at 38x.

blocks.text: Accent turns imported wood pulp into MCC by acid hydrolysis and drying, in 22 grades, and upgrades part of it into premium silicified MCC (SMCC) and MCC Spheres for slow-release capsules. The Dahej SEZ plant (7,200 MTPA, spray-dried) serves exports; Pirana (2,000 MTPA, spin-flash dried) serves India and handles traded volumes. About 85% of sales go through distributors.

blocks.text: Management opens each call by saying it gives no forward-looking guidance, then gives dates and revenue figures in the Q&A. The plant dates have slipped every time; margin and cash promises have been kept.

items.text: Promoters (16 holders, led by the four Patel directors) held 55.5% at Mar 2026 and 51.4% at Sep 2026 with no new shares issued, so about 4% of the company was sold or transferred; no pledge.
Domestic institutions fell from 3.6% to 2.4%; about 3,400 shareholders.

FY26 purchases from promoter-linked firms were ₹46.2 Cr (Maccent Bio Care ₹16.5 Cr, Accent Biosciences ₹12.5 Cr, Jainishk ₹11.5 Cr, Brohks ₹5.6 Cr), about half of the ₹95 Cr of traded goods; sales to them were ₹23.9 Cr.
The four promoter-directors were paid ₹1.46 Cr each (₹5.8 Cr in all, +12%), 47 times the median employee.
Contingent liabilities include a ₹4.1 Cr Gujarat Pollution Control Board appeal and ₹15.3 Cr of EPCG export obligations.
Auditors (TR Chadha & Co) made revenue cut-off and the ₹102 Cr Unit III work in progress key audit matters.
Investors said they heard of the Unit III delay from credit ratings and plant visits before any filing; no call was held for H1 FY27.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

Accent is a profitable, debt-free MCC exporter with H1 FY27 showing what less trading and more premium products can do for margins. The stock already prices in Unit III working; the plant has missed every date given so far, and the related-party trading and promoter selling need explaining. The consent to operate for Phase 1 and the H2 margin are what to watch.
